doc.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

chapter: Current gigs and Goodman family stories
title: Fred Astaire's recording with Goodman: Who Cares
summary: Sol urges Monk to find Astaire's record with Goodman's sextet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: They were terrific. They were delicious. They were so good. A lot of times Benny Goodman was on the side and somebody else was conducting the band. I don’t remember who it was. He picked different guys to conduct the show for them dancers. One time he came out with his clarinet while they were dancing and he played the clarinet for them. It was so good. Do you have a record that Benny Goodman made with Fred Astaire called “Who Cares?” You ever hear that song?
George Gershwin wrote that song. Let me see if I remember. May I please? [Sol plays]. You ever hear that song?
It doesn’t sound familiar to me.

George Gershwin wrote that song “Who Cares.” And Fred Astaire made a recording of that with Benny Goodman’s band on Columbia Records. Great, great record, where he sang, and then he tap danced, and Benny Goodman’s sextet at that time with Lionel Hampton and Charlie Christian played the background for him, when he gave him a stop tempo like this Monk [Sol plays]. Then the band would come in. Oh, pick up that record if you can, will ya? And on the other side is another great song that Fred Astaire sang, and he danced, it was called “Just Like Taking Candy From a Baby.” Will you remember that or you want to write it down?

“Just Like Taking Candy From a Baby.” Great record. Great. Fred Astaire singing and dancing on both sides. And it’s so exciting, after he tap danced, the band came in. See he was tap dancing to the sextet. They gave him a stop time. Then the band came in like

gangbusters [scats]. Right, the band would come in on the second half [scats]. Get that record please. You’ll love it. You’ll thank me. Columbia Records. “Who Cares,” the other side is “Just Like Taking Candy From a Baby.”
Is it a 78 do you think?
Okay, well I may have it.
Yeah but they put it on an LP I know. But you — a very exciting record.
